# VAD test corpus

Deterministic, synthesized mono 48 kHz PCM16 WAV clips with exact
speech-region ground truth in `labels.csv` (`file,start_ms,end_ms`; ms
values come from the synthesis loop's frame counters, so they are exact
to one 10 ms frame). Everything is regenerated by:

    go run gen_corpus.go

from this directory (Go ≥1.23; the file carries a `//go:build ignore`
tag so it is not part of the package build).

## Synthesis parameters

All clips share a room-noise floor of one-pole lowpassed white noise
(filter coefficient 0.18), normalized to RMS 30 ≈ −60.8 dBFS.

| file | length | content |
|------|--------|---------|
| `speech_normal.wav` | 9.1 s | 3 speech episodes (8–9 syllables each), separated by 700 ms noise. Episode syllables normalized to RMS 300 ≈ −40.8 dBFS (+20 dB over floor). |
| `speech_soft.wav` | 6.4 s | 2 episodes at RMS 150 ≈ −46.8 dBFS (+14 dB over floor). |
| `silence_room.wav` | 5 s | noise floor only. |
| `keyboard.wav` | 8.5 s | click transients: 3 ms exponentially decaying bursts (τ = 2 ms, peak 20000, ≈ −14 dBFS in their frame) over the noise floor; deterministic 80–160 ms spacing with two fast-typing runs at 60 ms. |
| `music_background.wav` | 8 s | 4-tone chord (220 / 277.18 / 329.63 / 440 Hz), ±0.5 % frequency vibrato at 5 Hz (constant amplitude), 1 s noise lead, 1.2 s fade-in to sustained RMS 60 (+6 dB over floor), 3.5 s sustain, 1.3 s fade-out. |

Speech syllables: 120–180 ms, one-pole lowpassed noise with 15 % attack /
30 % release envelope, 60–90 ms gaps, per-syllable RMS normalization to
the episode level.

## Why these levels

The energy VAD defaults (open = noise floor +10 dB, clamped at −50 dBFS)
put every clip on the intended side of the threshold: speech ≥ +14 dB
opens, background music at +6 dB and transients (single-frame energy,
rejected by the 50 ms sustain requirement) do not. Sustained music at
speech level is a documented limitation of energy VADs (see
internal/audio/pipeline/vad.go); the corpus models realistic background
music, which the adaptive noise floor absorbs.
